newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to name date for first oil tender.
newsitem.headline: Germany to name date for first oil tender.

text.p: Germany will issue a statement later on Monday providing details of its planned sale of crude oil reserves, a government source told Reuters.
"The statement will say when the first tranche will be offered for sale, how much oil will be included in this first tender as well as the quality and type of oil," the source said.
Earlier an official of Germany's oil stocks agency said the country planned to hold the first tender in August of some 450,000 cubic metres, or around 2.8 million barrels, of oil.

There will be a total of up to six tenders as Germany unloads nearly two million tonnes of oil between August and the end of 1997, which is aimed at helping Bonn lower its budget deficit to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
The sale of the oil is being organised by the Hamburg-based agency EBV.
